title: Subtraction (2-digit)
description: Class 2 IMO — Subtraction of 2-digit numbers with and without borrowing, the link between addition and subtraction, and word problems for the Maths Olympiad.

topics.title: Subtracting Without Borrowing
topics.concept:
To subtract 2-digit numbers, subtract the ones first, then the tens. For 58 − 23: ones 8 − 3 = 5, tens 5 − 2 = 3, so the answer is 35.

Subtraction means take away or how many are left.
recap: Subtraction means take away / how many left.

topics.title: Subtracting With Borrowing
topics.concept: When the top ones digit is smaller, we borrow 1 ten from the tens place. For 52 − 27: ones 2 is smaller than 7, so borrow 1 ten — now 12 − 7 = 5, and tens become 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 25.
recap: If the top ones digit is too small, borrow 1 ten.
Borrowing makes the ones 10 more and the tens 1 less.

topics.title: Addition–Subtraction Link & Word Problems
topics.concept: Addition and subtraction are opposite operations. If 30 + 20 = 50, then 50 − 20 = 30. We can use addition to check subtraction. In word problems, words like left, how many more and remaining mean subtract.

examples.solution: Add back: 27 + 18 = 45. Yes, it is correct.

examples.problem: Amit had ₹50 and spent ₹35. How much is left?

recap: Subtraction undoes addition (and the other way round).
'Left / remaining / how many more' means subtract.
